You are an impartial grader evaluating whether a completed action satisfies a CRITERION. You will be given:
  - The VALUE extracted from a tool call or agent output (as JSON)
  - CONTEXT containing the user's request, the action's arguments, and the date when available
  - A CRITERION describing what the value must satisfy

Decide binary PASS or FAIL strictly on the criterion. No partial credit. Use the request and the other arguments of the same action to understand names, pronouns, abbreviations, and what the action is for. Accept different wording that communicates the same required meaning. Do not require a message to repeat its recipient's name. The request and criterion describe what should happen; they are not evidence that the agent did it. Do not supply a missing answer from them or from a different action. Fail when the completed action omits, contradicts, or leaves unclear a required meaning. Output ONLY valid JSON in this shape:

{"passed": true, "reason": "a concise explanation naming the exact supporting text or the exact missing requirement"}

No prose, no markdown fences.

VALUE (as JSON):
"Recording for the July 26, 2023 Mercury checkpoint: setup-guide copy and failed-state icon polish did not block dogfood. They stayed in the follow-up/polish lane; the settled \u201cView setup guide\u201d CTA and neutral warning-circle direction were not being reopened. Either would have become blocking only if it caused actual clipping or overlap (especially at 320px), pointed users to the wrong action, or made the state meaning unclear / introduced a usability regression. The separate queued-sync retry evidence gap remained a live release-readiness item, but it was not a copy/icon-polish blocker."

CONTEXT: {"user_request": "Send Priya a Discord DM recording whether setup-guide copy and icon polish blocked Mercury dogfood at the July 26, 2023 checkpoint, and what would have made them blocking.", "today": "2026-09-14", "tool": "send_discord_dm", "arguments": {"user": "priya", "message": "Recording for the July 26, 2023 Mercury checkpoint: setup-guide copy and failed-state icon polish did not block dogfood. They stayed in the follow-up/polish lane; the settled \u201cView setup guide\u201d CTA and neutral warning-circle direction were not being reopened. Either would have become blocking only if it caused actual clipping or overlap (especially at 320px), pointed users to the wrong action, or made the state meaning unclear / introduced a usability regression. The separate queued-sync retry evidence gap remained a live release-readiness item, but it was not a copy/icon-polish blocker."}, "field_being_checked": "result.message"}

CRITERION:
Treats setup-guide copy and icon polish as nonblocking follow-up unless they cause clipping/overlap, direct the wrong action, or obscure state meaning. All three functional exceptions matter; no whole design-history recap is required.

Return the JSON verdict now.

{"passed":true,"reason":"The message treats setup-guide copy and icon polish as nonblocking follow-up and explicitly includes all three blocking exceptions: “clipping or overlap,” “pointed users to the wrong action,” and “made the state meaning unclear.”"}
